page: Google Cloud Platform f1-micro is an entry-level, burstable virtual machine instance belonging to the f1 server family. It features a shared physical core architecture with 1 vCPU and 1 physical core based on the Intel Xeon x86_64 processor. The instance is configured with 0.6 GB of RAM, resulting in a memory density of 0.6 GB per core. It does not include any local storage or dedicated GPUs, and does not provide complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks place the f1-micro in the bottom 10% across all tested categories. The stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests both scored 384.79, reflecting the shared-core CPU allocation. Memory bandwidth is highly constrained, with a read-only small block cached speed of 80.8 GB/sec and a large block write speed of 0.2 GB/sec. Passmark CPU and memory scores are similarly low, with a CPU score of 236.08 and a database operations score of 0.0. Static web serving throughput is limited to 0.22 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the f1-micro offers a highly economical entry point for running basic services, though it presents significant resource tradeoffs. The shared CPU allocation and extremely low memory capacity of 0.6 GB make it unsuitable for resource-intensive tasks. Appropriate workloads are limited to lightweight background processes, simple cron jobs, low-traffic static web serving, and basic development or testing tasks that do not require sustained CPU or memory throughput.
description: Google Cloud Platform f1-micro is an entry-level, shared-core instance in the f1 family, designed for minimal resource requirements. It features 1 vCPU on a shared Intel Xeon physical core, 0.6 GB of RAM, and x86_64 architecture, with no local storage or GPU accelerators. Benchmark results consistently place this instance in the bottom 10% of performance, with a stress-ng CPU score of 384.79, a Passmark CPU score of 236.08, and static web serving throughput of 0.22 GB/sec. Due to the shared CPU allocation and highly constrained memory, the f1-micro is a cost-efficient option solely for lightweight, non-critical workloads. It is best suited for basic administrative tasks, simple cron jobs, low-traffic static web hosting, and minimal development environments.
